finding: Mixin constructor types use `any[]` args which is technically required by TypeScript's mixin pattern (TS2545), but lacks eslint-disable-next-line scoping in FormMixin.ts — the eslint-disable comment covers the entire file rather than the single line.
recommendation: Scope the eslint-disable to a single-line comment on the type alias line only: `// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` directly above `type Constructor<T = object> = new (...args: any[]) => T;`

finding: AriaDelegationMixin uses `as unknown as T` double cast at the return site — a necessary escape hatch for the mixin pattern, but the interface AriaDelegationMixinInterface is not intersected into the return type, requiring callers to cast instances themselves.
recommendation: Update the return type of `mixinDelegatesAria` to `T & Constructor<AriaDelegationMixinInterface>` and adjust the cast accordingly so callers receive typed ARIA accessors automatically without explicit casting.

finding: Test file uses `(el as any).columns` and `(el as any).rows` to bypass type checking when setting invalid values — these are test-boundary casts but `as any` is still forbidden by strict policy.
recommendation: Replace `as any` casts in tests with `as unknown as HxDataTable` or use a helper like `setProperty(el, 'columns', ...)` typed with `unknown`. Alternatively define a `TestHxDataTable` interface that widens the property types to `unknown` for invalid-value testing.

finding: Test file uses `(el as any)._elInternals` to access a private field for assertion — `as any` is used to escape type checking, violating the zero-`any` policy.
recommendation: Expose the internal role via a protected getter or use `@ts-expect-error` with a descriptive comment, or cast through `unknown`: `(el as unknown as { _elInternals: { role: string } })._elInternals?.role`.

finding: hx-split-button declares `override ariaLabel = ''` which directly shadows the native `HTMLElement.ariaLabel` property — the same anti-pattern that was already remediated in hx-action-bar. The rename to `accessibleLabel` was applied inconsistently.
recommendation: Rename the `ariaLabel` property to `accessibleLabel` with attribute `accessible-label` (matching the hx-action-bar pattern), add backward-compat deprecation warning in the setter, and update the React types in HxSplitButton/types.ts accordingly.

finding: hx-combobox declares `override ariaLabel: string | null = null` which shadows the native HTMLElement.ariaLabel property. Unlike hx-action-bar (already migrated), this component was not updated during the accessibleLabel remediation.
recommendation: Migrate `ariaLabel` to `accessibleLabel` with `attribute: 'accessible-label'`, emit a deprecation warning for the old attribute, and update HxCombobox/types.ts to use `accessibleLabel` instead of `ariaLabel`.

finding: hx-text-input declares `override ariaLabel: string | null = null` — same HTMLElement.ariaLabel shadowing anti-pattern as hx-combobox and hx-split-button. The remediation applied to hx-action-bar was not propagated to input components.
recommendation: Apply the same `accessibleLabel` / `accessible-label` migration as hx-action-bar. Update HxTextInput/types.ts, HxSelect/types.ts, HxTextarea/types.ts, and HxSteps/types.ts in hx-react simultaneously.

finding: HxComboboxProps still exposes `ariaLabel?: string | null` which reflects the un-migrated web component property. Once hx-combobox migrates to `accessibleLabel`, this type will be stale and will silently accept the wrong prop name.
recommendation: After migrating hx-combobox to `accessibleLabel`, update HxComboboxProps to expose `accessibleLabel?: string` and remove `ariaLabel`. Add a deprecated comment on `ariaLabel` if backward compat is needed during transition.

finding: HxSplitButtonProps uses `ariaLabel?: string` (non-nullable) while other components use `ariaLabel?: string | null` — the inconsistency creates a type mismatch between what the web component stores (empty string '') and what React consumers expect (string | undefined).
recommendation: Normalize all `ariaLabel` props to `string | null | undefined` if they reflect nullable web component properties, or make explicit that `undefined` is the absent state and the component coerces to a default.

finding: HxActionBarProps correctly uses `accessibleLabel?: string` reflecting the completed ariaLabel→accessibleLabel migration. The `sticky` deprecated prop is absent from types which is correct since it maps to `position` now.
HxButtonProps is well-typed: all union variants match the web component, `href` and `target` are correctly `string | undefined`, and `onHxClick` is typed as `(event: Event) => void`.

HxSwitchProps includes `validity?: ValidityState` and `validationMessage?: string` as writable props, but these are read-only getters on the web component — they should not be settable by React consumers and their presence may create confusion.
recommendation: Remove `validity` and `validationMessage` from HxSwitchProps since they are computed/read-only on the web component. Exposing them as settable props implies consumers can override them, which is incorrect.

finding: HxToggleButtonProps exposes `validity?: ValidityState` and `validationMessage?: string` as settable props — same pattern as HxSwitch. These are read-only computed properties on the web component.
recommendation: Remove `validity` and `validationMessage` from HxToggleButtonProps. If consumers genuinely need to read these values they should access the web component instance directly.

finding: HxTextInputProps exposes `form?: HTMLFormElement | null` as a settable prop, but `form` is a read-only computed getter on the web component (delegates to ElementInternals.form). Making it settable in the React types is misleading.
recommendation: Remove `form` from HxTextInputProps. It is not a settable web component property. Consumers should use the standard `form` HTML attribute (a string referencing a form id) rather than an HTMLFormElement instance.

finding: HxFileUploadProps exposes `files?: File[]` as a settable prop, but this is a read-only getter on the web component that returns a copy of the internal file list. Setting it has no effect.
recommendation: Remove `files` from HxFileUploadProps or mark it clearly as read-only with a JSDoc `@readonly` comment and rename to avoid implying settability, e.g. use a ref-based approach if consumers need to read files.

finding: HxTimePickerProps is clean: `format` is correctly typed as `'12h' | '24h'` union, all other props are appropriately typed with correct optionality.
HxPhiFieldProps correctly types `fieldType` as a union literal and `data` as string. PHI-specific props are well-documented with security guidance.

hx-button uses `PropertyValues<this>` in updated(), typed CustomEvent<{originalEvent: MouseEvent}>, proper union types for variant/size/type, HTMLElementTagNameMap and HTMLElementEventMap both declared.

hx-alert is well-typed with typed CustomEvent detail, proper null checks, union types for variant. Minor: `_defaultSeverityLabel` uses `Record<string, string>` for the labels map — should use `Record<AlertVariant, string>` to be exhaustive and benefit from compiler coverage.
recommendation: Change `const labels: Record<string, string>` to `const labels: Record<AlertVariant, string>` so TypeScript enforces all variants are handled and the `?? ''` fallback becomes unnecessary dead code.

finding: hx-action-bar demonstrates best-practice patterns: proper mixin usage, `??` nullish coalescing, optional chaining, roving tabindex implemented without any `any` or non-null assertions, HTMLElementTagNameMap declared.

HelixElement base class is exemplary: uses private class fields (#internals), properly guards formAssociated before accessing _internals, all hook methods use underscore-prefixed unused params (_disabled, _state, _mode), no any usage.

tsconfig.base.json enables `strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, `forceConsistentCasingInFileNames`, and `declarationMap`, but is missing `noImplicitReturns`, `noFallthroughCasesInSwitch`, and `noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature` from the documented enterprise strict config.
recommendation: Add `"noImplicitReturns": true`, `"noFallthroughCasesInSwitch": true`, and `"noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature": true` to tsconfig.base.json. These are documented as required in CLAUDE.md strict mode configuration.

finding: tsconfig.json in hx-library correctly sets `declaration: true`, `declarationMap: true`, `sourceMap: true`, `composite: true`, and excludes test/stories files from the declaration output. The hx-library/src/index.ts is well-structured with all components and types re-exported.

hx-react/tsconfig.json extends tsconfig.base.json and sets `declarationDir: dist` but lacks `composite: true` and `declaration: true` — these must be inherited from the base config rather than explicit, which is valid but makes the intent less clear and may cause issues if the base config is ever modified.
recommendation: Add `"composite": true` and `"declaration": true` explicitly to packages/hx-react/tsconfig.json to make the project reference configuration self-documenting and resilient to base config changes.

finding: hx-library/src/index.ts exports inconsistent naming patterns: some components export both `Helix*` class and legacy `Hx*`/`Wc*` type aliases (e.g., `HxBadge`, `WcBadge`, `HxSwitch`, `WcSwitch`, `WcTag`, `HxTag`) while most don't. This creates a confused public API surface with two naming schemes.
recommendation: Audit and document the intentional `Hx*`/`Wc*` re-exports. If they exist only for backward compat, add `@deprecated` JSDoc. If they are unintentional duplicates, remove them and clean up consumer callsites. Standardize on `Helix*` class names as the public API.

finding: The custom-elements.json (28019 lines) is generated and comprehensive. However, because `accessibleLabel` was added to hx-action-bar but `ariaLabel` was not yet migrated in hx-combobox, hx-text-input, and hx-split-button, the CEM reflects an inconsistent API surface across components.
recommendation: Complete the ariaLabel→accessibleLabel migration across all affected components before the next CEM regeneration so the manifest reflects a consistent naming convention. Run `pnpm run cem` after migration.

finding: hx-react/src/index.ts exports all components and their props types correctly — 90+ components with named exports following `HxComponent` / `HxComponentProps` convention. All modified types files reviewed are complete.

FormMixin and FocusMixin use well-constrained generics: `TBase extends Constructor<HelixElement>` prevents mixing into non-HelixElement classes, and the return type intersects `TBase & Constructor<FormMixinInterface>` for correct type inference.

Event handler callbacks in hx-react types are typed as `(event: Event) => void` uniformly — losing CustomEvent detail type information. Consumers cannot access `event.detail` without a type assertion.
recommendation: Type event callbacks with their specific CustomEvent detail type: e.g. `onHxClick?: (event: CustomEvent<{ originalEvent: MouseEvent }>) => void`. This requires defining detail interfaces in the react types package or re-exporting them from hx-library.

finding: TypeScript quality across the HELiX codebase is generally strong: zero @ts-ignore usage, HTMLElementTagNameMap declared on all sampled components, PropertyValues<this> used correctly in lifecycle methods, and mixin patterns are well-typed with appropriate generic constraints. The primary issues are: (1) incomplete ariaLabel→accessibleLabel migration creating shadow-property violations across hx-combobox, hx-text-input, and hx-split-button; (2) React event callbacks typed as base Event rather than typed CustomEvent<Detail>, losing detail type safety for consumers; (3) tsconfig.base.json missing three documented strict flags (noImplicitReturns, noFallthroughCasesInSwitch, noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature); (4) two `as any` casts in test files; (5) read-only web component getters (validity, validationMessage, form, files) exposed as settable props in several React types files.
recommendation: Top 3 fixes: (1) Complete the ariaLabel→accessibleLabel migration on hx-combobox, hx-text-input, hx-select, hx-textarea, hx-steps, and hx-split-button to eliminate HTMLElement property shadowing; (2) Add noImplicitReturns and noFallthroughCasesInSwitch to tsconfig.base.json to match the documented enterprise strict configuration; (3) Type hx-react event callbacks with specific CustomEvent<Detail> signatures rather than base Event, unlocking type-safe event.detail access for React consumers.
